predecessors.name: Kingdom of Dali
predecessors.text: the Dali Kingdom's land, of which the Duan kept the Dali district after the surrender of 1256

ledger.x: 1256: Duan Xingzhi surrenders to the Mongols and is enfeoffed as Maharaja of Dali.
1274: Ajall Shams al-Din reorganises Yunnan and the Duan rule becomes a hereditary tusi governor-generalship.
1382: Ming forces attack Duan Shi's realm.
February 1383: the last Dali stronghold falls.
February 1383: the Duan governors of Dali end with the fall of Dengchuan; the family goes to Nanjing and Dali passes to the Ming.

wars.name: Ming conquest of Yunnan
wars.outcome: Ming victory: Basalawarmi dies on 6 January 1382, Duan Shi's realm is crushed in 1382 and the last Dali stronghold, Dengchuan, falls in February 1383.

wars.name: Mongol conquest of Dali
wars.outcome: The Mongols conquer Dali in 1253 (the column converge on the city in late 1253), take Dali and Shanchan after two more years and Duan Xingzhi surrenders in 1256: the origin of the Duan governors.

certainty.note: A hereditary vassal district whose extent no page gives; a circle round Dali stands for it.
